subject: Re: Request for IR runbook, SIG mapping and artifact package
messages:
From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@finservco.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: secureops@finservco.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request for IR runbook, SIG mapping and artifact package

Hi Olga,

Following up from our compliance sync earlier — FinServCo’s Audit team needs a copy of Redwood’s incident response runbook and the SIG-to-control mapping that you produced for SOC 2. Specifically they asked for: 

- The current IR runbook (PDF) with escalation paths and RTO/RPO guidance.
- A SIG response matrix that maps SIG questions to artifacts we can provide.
- A short artifact package (logs, retained evidence list) for an example recent event so they can validate lineage.

Are you able to provide these by EOD Wednesday (11/11)? If not, please propose alternate timeline. We also want a brief note summarizing whether any of the artifacts contain customer-identifiable data and your recommended redaction steps.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Morris
Security & Compliance, FinServCo
alice.morris@finservco.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@finservco.com>
Cc: secureops@finservco.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for IR runbook, SIG mapping and artifact package

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. I can get you the runbook and a SIG mapping snapshot. A couple of notes up front:

- I will attach the runbook v2.1 (internal draft) and a working SIG response matrix. The matrix maps each SIG question to the artifact type we can produce (logs, console traces, runbook excerpts, configuration snapshots).
- The full forensic logs contain tokenized identifiers; we will provide a sanitized summary file and a separate redaction plan.
- Timeline: I will send the runbook and SIG matrix today, and the sanitized log summary by EOD Wednesday (11/11). If you need raw logs under an NDA, we can coordinate with your legal team.

Attached: IR_Runbook_v2.1.pdf (draft), SIG_Response_Matrix.xlsx (workbook).

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for IR runbook, SIG mapping and artifact package

Olga — reviewed the runbook and the escalation paths look correct. A few small edits I recommend (will incorporate into a v2.1.1):

- Clarify secondary paging contact after 30 minutes for regional on-call (APAC/EU flows).
- Add explicit step to rotate credentials used in forensic collections when an account compromise is suspected.
- Confirmed retention for request: we keep structured traces for 90 days, cold storage for 2 years. We can produce aggregated traces for FinServCo without customer IDs.

For the sanitized logs: we can provide a concise forensic-log-summary (attached) that contains time series, affected services, and redaction notes. Raw bucket-level logs require an NDA and a signed DPA addendum.

I’ll attach the sanitized summary once I finish redaction notes.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Ops Manager
[Attachment: forensic-log-summary-20261110.txt (text/plain)]

From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@finservco.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: secureops@finservco.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for IR runbook, SIG mapping and artifact package

Olga / Naomi — this is perfect, thank you. A couple follow-ups from our auditors:

1) Can you add a short statement confirming whether any of the attached artifacts (runbook, SIG matrix, sanitized summary) reference customer PII or transaction-level identifiers? If none, please state that explicitly.
2) For the retention statement, please confirm the exact S3 paths (or buckets) where the cold storage traces reside so our auditors can reference them in their checklist.
3) If an NDA is required for raw buckets, please send the contact at Redwood Legal or an intake link so we can start that process.

If you can answer 1–3 in a short email, we can close out the SOC 2 evidence request by midday Thursday.

Thanks again — Alice

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@finservco.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for IR runbook, SIG mapping and artifact package

Alice — short answers below so auditors have a single record: 

1) Customer-identifiable data: none of the attached artifacts (IR_Runbook_v2.1.pdf, SIG_Response_Matrix.xlsx, forensic-log-summary-20261110.txt) contain customer PII or transaction-level identifiers. The forensic-log-summary is an aggregated/sanitized export with tokenized IDs; we include a redaction appendix describing what was removed.

2) Retention S3 paths: cold storage traces are held in s3://redwood-logs/cold-traces/ (role-based access). Aggregated traces for evidence are staged under s3://redwood-evidence/for-audits/finservco-2026-11/ (read access granted via signed DPA/NDA).

3) NDA / legal intake: please use our legal intake form (https://legal.redwood.com/intake) — I’ve also copied Karthik for DPA coordination. Karthik, our contact for quick NDAs is legal-intake@redwood.com; we typically use the standard DPA addendum in DocuSign (I can generate if you prefer).

Next steps: I will upload the final sanitized bundle to the evidence staging path and share a Drive link by EOD. Let me know if you need a short cover letter for your auditors.

Regards — Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
